items.title: Office Hours: Recapping Ignite in Cabo San Lucas
items.author: Brent Ozar Unlimited
items.summary:
I discuss the surprisingly light database news coming out of the Microsoft Ignite conference, then answer your top-voted questions from https://pollgab.com/room/brento.

00:00 Start
01:16 News: Microsoft Ignite didn't have much database news
02:00 News: Cross-database query support in Azure SQL DB Hyperscale
03:55 News: SSMS Copilot experience reworked again
06:51 Stewpeas: Hi Brent, I'm mid twenties and 3 years into my DBA journey. I love my job and geek out over SQL Server internals and performance tuning. I'm terrified that in 5-10 years there will be no need for a DBA other than a feeling of safety for HA/DR. Any advice about what to learn next?
08:48 flyboy91901: With SQL Server 2025 Microsoft has mentioned this is the last version with SSIS.  What is the direction one should look at for ETLs for on-prem use? MSFT response is unclear.
10:48 database: As a large enterprise, we are looking to slowly migrate towards PostgreSQL (e.g. Strangler Pattern) and away from SQL Server. Is PostgreSQL on Azure still a "meme" product compared to Aurora? What is your personal experience and what should we consider going into our research?
12:40 Ozzie1527: Glad to hear that you enjoyed this years PASS Summit. How should you compare it against this years SQL Bits and what are the prons and cons of both of them?
15:51 Nestrus: What would be your rough outline for a DB2DB interface? E.g., would you use RSCI or table hints for the communication table to minimize waiting on locks and would you "just" use Linked Server or would you prefer to access the remote table via a own, separate tool (to avoid DTC)?
17:30 Asking_for_a_friend: Is there a reason t sql will not take a hint to use an index to create a clustered index. A unique nonclustered index 'Tmp' was created in six hours to test run time & resource load. Creating a unique clustered index 'PKCl', the real goal, it skipped 'Tmp' & ran from scratch

items.title: Databricks Unity Gateway in Five Minutes
items.author: Advancing Analytics
items.summary:
How do you manage multiple AI models, control costs and apply governance without making everything more complicated? Unity Gateway is the answer!

In this quick-fire demo, Gavi and Sepi walk through Databricks Unity Gateway, showing how to manage AI models, configure guardrails and control access to the tools your AI agents use. All in around five minutes.

From switching between LLM providers to setting budgets and configuring model fallbacks, here's a practical look at what Unity Gateway can do.

In this video, you'll learn:
- Model providers: How to connect external LLM providers like Anthropic and Azure alongside Databricks-hosted models.
- Model routing: How to switch between models without changing your application code.
- Fallbacks & budgets: How to manage costs, split traffic and configure fallback models.
- AI guardrails: How to apply policies for PII detection, jailbreak protection and other safeguards.
- MCP governance: How to control which tools your AI agents can access, including granular read/write permissions.
- Unity Catalog integration: How to govern agent skills alongside your other assets.

Chapters:

00:00 Introduction to Databricks Unity Gateway
00:59 Getting started with Unity Gateway
01:13 Connecting external model providers
02:25 Configuring Databricks-hosted and external models
03:19 Model routing and switching between LLMs
04:11 Managing model fallbacks and budgets
04:38 Setting up AI guardrails and policies
05:06 Governing MCP tools and permissions
06:16 Managing AI agent skills with Unity Catalog
07:05 Unity Gateway vs AI Gateway: What's changed?
08:00 Favourite features: Budgets and model fallbacks
09:11 Wrap-up and what's next

Got questions?

Want a deeper dive into a particular Unity Gateway feature? Drop your questions in the comments and let us know what you'd like us to cover next.
